text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Cooperation with the EU is the priority of Yugoslavia's foreign policy, says Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic in the European parliament.

- Yugoslavia will maintain its stands regarding the succession of the former Yugoslavia at the next round of talks on the issue scheduled for December 3 and 4 in Brussels, the federal government decided.
- Yugoslavia expects to earn $550 million from food exports by the end of the year, says Serbian agricultural ministry.
- Novi Sad oil company Naftagas abandons oil drilling in Valdanos on the Montenegrin coast after failing to find commercial quantities of oil and will move to Vojvodina.
- The Yugoslav federal government examined a bill providing for payment operations to go solely through commercial banks.
- Yugoslav bankers supported the country's 1997 restrictive monetary policy in order to maintain a stable exchange rate of the domestic currency and stabilise prices.
- The country needs to carry out reforms of its Post and Telecommunication system and carry out ownership transformation, said Yugoslavia's PTT general manager Milorad Jaksic.
- Belgraders to chose 55 councillors in the municipal assembly in the third round of local elections.
- Seventh day of protests against annullment of local election results in Serbia, demonstrators determined to persevere.
- Belgrade lawyers decide to "freeze" their seven day protest until December 20 and return to courts.

- The municipal election commission asks Nasa Borba to respect 48-hour electoral silence. The paper answers it is only covering citizns' demonstrations and quotes headlines in pro-government papers which hail the Socialists' alleged victory.
- The president of the Serbian Radical Party (SRS) Vojislav Seselj will be the new president of Zemun municipality, where radicals won majority in local elections.
- Regular bus line Belgrade-Zagreb via the highway between the two cities is due to start operating Wednesday.

- Yugoslav mining-metallurgy complex Trepca exports two thirds of its production says director Novak Bijelic. Its production has reached the value of over one billion dinars in less than two years and foreign exchange income of $91.706 he says. -- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 4275
